clue.text: 0 cold 'eart cries falsely!

indicators.note: cries made falsely are put on, so these letters are rearranged into a false version

parts.note: the figure 0 stands for the letter O, which it resembles

explanation.surface: A sentimental lament in dropped-aitch Cockney about a cold heart, delivered insincerely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falsely' shuffles O (the 0), COLD, 'EART and CRIES into the answer, and the whole clue also describes it: a cold heart weeping falsely. 'Eart is Cockney for heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocodiles were fabled to weep while devouring prey, so their tears are proverbial insincere sorrow.

clue.text: Change in order to get back to mountains

parts.note: the back of something is its rear
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: Instructions to alter your plans so you can return to the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter the order or arrangement of things is to rearrange them.

clue.text: Beast removing good books from Arthur's place

indicators.note: removing tells us to take letters away from the place named

parts.note: Camelot was King Arthur's legendary court
OT is the Old Testament, books of the Good Book

explanation.surface: An animal that throws the scriptures out of King Arthur's castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A camel is a large desert animal, a beast of burden.

clue.text: Foul play? I'd try different occupation

indicators.note: different asks for the letters of the words before it in another order

parts.note: an occupation is one's work

explanation.surface: Someone suspecting foul play resolves to change careers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty work is underhand, dishonest dealing, which is what foul play means.

clue.text: Car plant

explanation.definitionFit: Lotus is a British sports-car maker, and the lotus is a water lily revered in Asia.

clue.text: Last man in for tax cut with capital in Icelandic bank?

indicators.note: cut means the word for tax loses its final letter
the capital of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a bank is a lender of money

explanation.surface: Suggests a tax cut tied to money parked in a bank in Iceland, recalling the 2008 banking crash.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the TAIL-ENDER is one of the weak batsmen who go in last; 'Last man in' points there, not at finance.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the lowest-order batsmen come in at the end of the innings, hence the final batter.

clue.text: Region around pole is field of conflict

indicators.note: around means the region word wraps the pole letter

parts.note: a region is an area
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A polar region described as a battleground.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a place of combat, from the Roman amphitheatre.

clue.text: American turning up with dirty bear

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the American abbreviation is read bottom to top

parts.note: to dirty something is to stain it

explanation.surface: An American with a filthy bear.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a weight or loss is to support or endure it.

clue.text: Be frugal with pickle

explanation.definitionFit: To scrape by is to live thriftily, and a scrape, like a pickle, is an awkward predicament.

clue.text: Big break for little boy at end of term

parts.note: Chas is a short form of the boy's name Charles

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word term

explanation.surface: A schoolboy's long holiday when term ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasm is a deep gap or rift, a huge break in the ground.

clue.text: They keep servants

explanation.definitionFit: Retainers are fees or devices that hold something in place, and retainers are also old household attendants.

clue.text: A universal recovery, so we hear

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal
a rally is a recovery, as in prices

explanation.surface: Reports of a worldwide economic upturn, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done by ear is done through hearing, so we take it in by listening.

clue.text: 24 changing name — a composer

indicators.note: changing asks for the letters of the cross-referenced answer in a new order

parts.note: the answer to 24 down

explanation.surface: A cross-reference changes a name and becomes a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedrich Smetana was the Czech composer of Ma Vlast.

clue.text: Painter from Germany in western state

indicators.note: in shows the answer is tucked inside the words western state

explanation.surface: A German artist living in an American western state.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German-born Dada and Surrealist artist.

clue.text: Limits of washing dirt makes terribly apparent?

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of dirt makes are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Grime clearly shows where somebody stopped washing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a description too: dirt plainly shows the lines where washing stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidemarks are grimy lines left on skin or a bath at the edge of where water reached.

clue.text: Government official with order to shoot -war-torn country's taken aback

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
a bud is a young shoot on a plant

indicators.note: taken aback means the country word is read backwards

parts.note: 'Nam is slang for Vietnam, torn by war; the 's adds the S

explanation.surface: An official told to fire on a country ravaged by war is shocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like surprise but turns 'NAM'S around, the 's giving its S.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman is an appointed public official who investigates citizens' complaints against authorities.

clue.text: Horses given drink somewhere in London

parts.note: bays are reddish-brown horses
water is a drink

explanation.surface: Horses watered at some London spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Bayswater is a district of west London north of Hyde Park.

clue.text: Shabby cat turns up with his head tucked in

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the cat word reads upwards

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: head picks the first letter of his

parts.note: to tuck in is to eat heartily, so tucked in means eaten

explanation.surface: A scruffy cat appears with its head tucked under.
explanation.definitionFit: Moth-eaten describes something worn and tatty, like cloth damaged by moths.

clue.text: Fine old clue is repeated, incorporating feedback

indicators.note: incorporating means the repeated pair takes in a letter
is repeated means the old-clue pair occurs twice

parts.note: a key is a clue to solving something
read as feed back: the back, or last letter, of feed

explanation.surface: Approval of a stale clue being reused, with feedback taken on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feedback' is not a response here: split it as 'feed back', the last letter of feed. 'incorporating' puts that D between the two OKEYs.
explanation.definitionFit: Okey-dokey is a jaunty colloquial way of saying all right or agreed.

clue.text: Talking pompously, addressing sailor?

parts.note: O is the vocative used when addressing someone, as in O king
a rating is a non-commissioned sailor

explanation.surface: Someone speaking grandly while talking to a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'O, rating!', the old way of addressing a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak in a grand, declamatory way.

clue.text: It goes round, just the same

indicators.note: just the same signals that the word reads identically backwards and forwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something that keeps turning and never changes.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, such as a helicopter's blades.

clue.text: Take exception to 14 being confused about east

indicators.note: about means those mixed letters go around the east letter
being confused means the cross-referenced letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 14 across

explanation.surface: Someone offended by a muddled cross-reference about the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being confused' turns ERNST into RESNT, and 'about' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitter or indignant about it.

clue.text: Island in swirling stream for Greek goddess

indicators.note: in means the island letter sits inside the mixed letters
swirling suggests the letters of stream are stirred about

explanation.surface: A goddess found on an island amid a swirling current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' makes ARTEMS from STREAM; 'in' puts I between its M and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis was the Greek goddess of hunting and the moon.

clue.text: Italian poet, extremely sensuous in a religious way

indicators.note: in places the extreme letters inside the religious way

parts.note: the Tao is the Way in Taoism

indicators.note: extremely picks the first and last letters of sensuous

explanation.surface: An Italian poet whose sensuality is religious in tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso wrote the Renaissance epic Gerusalemme Liberata.

clue.text: Old engine-driver, second to join crew

parts.note: a crew is a team

explanation.surface: A retired train driver's mate joining the railway crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam power drove the old locomotives, so it literally drove the engine.

clue.text: Time to get in drinks — point made by one in court

indicators.note: to get in means the time letter goes into the drinks word

parts.note: wines are drinks
S is south, a compass point

explanation.surface: Time to buy a round, a point made by someone at court.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness gives evidence at a trial in a court of law.

clue.text: Drunk held firmly

explanation.definitionFit: Tight is slang for intoxicated, and something tight is gripped securely.

clue.text: Home Secretary's first pressing rebel

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of Secretary's

parts.note: pressing means urgent

explanation.surface: The Home Secretary's first urgent task is dealing with a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is a person rising in revolt against authority.

clue.text: Board in advance

explanation.definitionFit: To get on a bus is to board it, and to get on is to make progress.

clue.text: Helpers do anagram — so it's sorted!

indicators.note: sorted means the letters before it are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A self-referential note that the anagram has been solved.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in it's is ignored; its S counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Good Samaritans are people who help strangers, after the parable in Luke's gospel.
